title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A scammer used a fake AI-generated website to display false account balances to a cryptocurrency trading app user, creating the appearance that his investments were growing when they were not. The website was a deception layer placed between the legitimate trading app and the user's view of his account. The victim made initial small trades and withdrawals that succeeded, establishing false confidence before larger sums disappeared.

The failure was in the user's ability to verify what he was seeing. The scammer exploited the difficulty of authenticating account information when a fabricated interface sits between the user and the real system. It is not established whether the trading app itself had security flaws, whether the user was directed to the fake website through social engineering, or what technical methods enabled the scammer to intercept or replace the legitimate display.

What would have caught this: account verification through a channel outside the app itself, such as a text message or email directly from the trading platform confirming balances or withdrawal requests. The victim's children are raising funds because authorities report these schemes rarely result in asset recovery.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, initially allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts to build trust. Over time, the investments grew larger. When Jerry tried to withdraw more money last week, he discovered the funds were gone and called police.

Investigators found that while the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false account balances on Jerry's screen. The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, lost their entire life savings in the scheme. Though working with Gwinnett County police, authorities say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe to help the couple pay for daily expenses, and the Dunaways are speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics criminals use to manipulate victims.
